title: Go: Profiling with pprof
description: Use Go's pprof tool to profile CPU, memory, and goroutine usage to optimize program performance.

steps.title: CPU profiling with pprof
steps.description: Write a CPU-intensive function (e.g., computing Fibonacci recursively). Start a CPU profile with `pprof.StartCPUProfile(f)` and stop with `pprof.StopCPUProfile()`. Write profile to a file and print a summary using `fmt.Printf("CPU profile written to %s\n", filename)`.
hints: Start CPU profile before the work, stop after
Profile file can be viewed with go tool pprof

verification.failureMessage: Print the filename where the CPU profile was saved.

steps.title: Memory (heap) profiling
steps.description: Allocate many objects (e.g., create a large slice of structs). Write a heap profile using `pprof.Lookup("heap").WriteTo(f, 0)`. Print the number of allocations using `fmt.Printf("Allocations: %d\n", allocs)`.
hints: heap profile shows live and historic allocations
WriteTo with debug=0 writes compressed protobuf

verification.failureMessage: Print the number of allocations from the heap profile.

steps.title: Goroutine profile
steps.description: Launch 5 goroutines that sleep briefly. Write a goroutine profile with `pprof.Lookup("goroutine").WriteTo(f, 2)`. The debug=2 format shows full stack traces. Print the goroutine count using `fmt.Printf("Goroutines: %d\n", count)`.
hints: Goroutine profile shows all current goroutine stacks
debug=1: plain text, debug=2: with function args
Look for "goroutine " prefix lines to count

verification.failureMessage: Print the number of active goroutines.

steps.title: Benchmark with memory stats
steps.description: Write a benchmark function `BenchmarkHeavy` that allocates memory. Track allocations with `testing.AllocsPerOp` or `b.ReportAllocs()`. Print benchmark results using `fmt.Printf("Benchmark: %d ns/op, %d allocs/op\n", ns, allocs)`.

verification.failureMessage: Print benchmark duration and allocation count.
